claim: For linear regression, the quantum algorithm runs in O~(r*sqrt(mn)/epsilon + n^3) time versus O~(mr + n^3) classically (Corollary 23).
paper: Accelerating Regression Tasks with Quantum Algorithms (arXiv:2509.24757 / OpenReview TBSyYj4VV6)
method: Leverage-score sparsifier; LS optimum on sketch compared to full optimum; m-scaling timed; asymptotic ordering symbolic.
reason: Sparsifier preserves LS optimum: loss_ratio=0.010<=0.15, gram rel-err=0.100<=0.15. Classical LS solve slope in m = 1.02 (linear), sketch solve slope = -0.31 (m-independent). Quantum/classical cost -> 0 as m->inf. EVIDENCE BOUNDARY: literal quantum construction needs QRAM/quantum hardware, NOT executed on CPU; shown via classical surrogate + symbolic limit.

mutation.description: (M1) s<r/eps^2 breaks optimum-preservation; (M2) tighter eps needs more samples; (M3) quantum sqrt(m) required for speedup.
